sss.s: Are the SEO tools really free?
sss.c: Yes. All tools are free and you don't need an account or an email address to use them. To prevent abuse there is a per-minute and daily usage limit for each tool.

sss.c: No. The address is used only to run the check; it is not written to a database or to logs. We only count how many times each tool is used per day.

sss.s: What if I want a more thorough analysis?
sss.c: The “Get a full analysis of the site” button below every result takes you to the free Site Analysis Report with the address already filled in; it scores your site's speed, SEO, content, technical setup, security and AI visibility from 0 to 100.

sss.s: Can I get the result by email?

sss.s: How long should the title and description be?
sss.c: Google truncates by pixel width, not characters. Roughly 30–60 character widths for the title and 70–160 for the description are safe; the tool counts wide characters such as Chinese as two.

sss.s: Why does the canonical tag matter?
sss.c: If the same content is reachable at several URLs, the canonical tells Google which one is the main page, so ranking signals are consolidated on one URL and duplicate-content issues are avoided.

sss.s: What size should the share image be?
sss.c: The safest size is 1200×630 pixels (about 1.91:1). Images smaller than 200×200 are not shown at all on many platforms; the file should be under 5 MB and served over https.

sss.s: I changed the tags but the share still looks old. Why?
sss.c: Social networks cache previews. Re-scrape the URL with Facebook's Sharing Debugger or LinkedIn's Post Inspector to refresh the cache.

sss.s: Does structured data improve rankings directly?
sss.c: It is not a direct ranking signal, but it makes pages eligible for rich results such as stars, FAQs and product prices, and helps AI search understand your page correctly.

sss.s: Does this replace Google's Rich Results Test?
sss.c: No; it is a quick pre-check of the basic rules. We recommend validating with Google's Rich Results Test before publishing as well.

sss.s: Does a page blocked by robots.txt drop out of the index?
sss.c: No. robots.txt only blocks crawling; a page linked from elsewhere can stay indexed. To remove it from the index, the page must be crawlable and carry noindex.

sss.s: Should I block AI crawlers?
sss.c: It depends on your business. Blocking GPTBot, ClaudeBot or PerplexityBot reduces how often your content appears in AI answers; leave them open if you want that visibility.

sss.s: Which pages belong in a sitemap?
sss.c: Only canonical URLs that return 200 and that you want indexed. Redirected pages, 404s and pages carrying noindex should not be in the sitemap.

sss.s: Is the lastmod field required?
sss.c: It is optional, but when it is accurate Google notices changed pages sooner. Use W3C format (e.g. 2026-10-01 or 2026-10-01T10:00:00+03:00) and the real modification date.

sss.s: What is the difference between 301 and 302?
sss.c: 301 (and 308) is permanent: search engines adopt the new URL and pass ranking signals. 302 (and 307) is temporary; use a permanent redirect for site moves and https migrations.

sss.s: How many redirects are too many?
sss.c: One step is ideal. Every extra step slows the page down and wastes crawl budget; Google stops following after 10 hops, but even chains longer than two steps should be fixed.

sss.s: Do security headers affect SEO?
sss.c: They are not a direct ranking signal, but HTTPS and user safety are part of Google's page experience, and a compromised site can be shown with a warning in search results.

sss.s: Will adding a CSP break my site?
sss.c: A wrong policy can block scripts. Try it first in report-only mode with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only, fix the violations, then switch to enforcing mode.

sss.s: What happens when an SSL certificate expires?
sss.c: Browsers show visitors a full-page security warning, most people leave and traffic and sales drop immediately. Check regularly that automatic renewal works.

sss.s: Is a free certificate good enough?
sss.c: For most sites, yes. Free certificates such as Let's Encrypt provide the same encryption; what matters is that automatic renewal and the intermediate chain are set up correctly.

sss.s: Can a page have more than one H1?
sss.c: Technically yes, but stating the page's main topic with one clear H1 is the most understandable structure for both visitors and search engines.

sss.s: Is skipping a heading level a problem?
sss.c: Search engines don't penalise it, but jumping from H2 to H4 makes the structure harder to follow for screen reader users. Choose levels by meaning and use CSS for the visual size.

sss.s: What is the ideal keyword density?
sss.c: There is no fixed ratio; Google doesn't look for a specific percentage. A phrase taking up more than 3% of the text, or a single word more than 5%, usually reads as unnatural. Covering the topic naturally with synonyms and related phrases works better.

sss.s: Why do Turkish texts need special care?
sss.c: Many tools lowercase a capital “I” to “i” and turn “İ” into a dotted combined character, so “IŞIK” and “ışık” or “İSTANBUL” and “istanbul” are counted as different words. This tool applies I→ı and İ→i correctly on Turkish pages and removes stop words such as “ve, bir, için”.

sss.s: Where should the target keyword appear?
sss.c: Using it naturally in the page title, the H1 and the first paragraph makes the topic clear; having it in the meta description and the URL helps clicks. Don't force it: readability always comes first.
